quotes.text: The house is H-shaped with 6 really perfect gables; the front gable (recently well rebuilt) is dated 1786 and shows the holbol style at its most beautiful, with convex edge mouldings continued onto the gable face and ending as fully developed scrolls, the nucleus of this farm consisted of the third of the 4 parts into which Vergelegen was divided after the recall of Willem Adriaan van der Stel; it was bought by Jacques Malan.
quotes.page: SAHRA identifier 9/2/083/0006, description column of the Helderberg heritage-site table. A register description is not paginated.

measurements.name: gable_count
measurements.note: Six gables on an H-plan house. This is the one countable architectural figure the whole Cape cluster's register descriptions produced, and it is worth what it says: the node's prose treats the CENTRE gable of the front as the type's carrier, and the register is counting six, which on an H-plan means the front centre plus the gable ends of the four wing arms and one more the description does not locate.

measurements.name: front_gable_date
measurements.as_printed: the front gable (recently well rebuilt) is dated 1786
measurements.note: A YEAR, not a dimension, and therefore carried with NO `value` and NO `unit`: the vocabulary has neither, and writing 1786 as a `count` would let a numeric check agree with a count of something. Recorded because the node's own prose makes the dated gable a defining habit -- 'a shaped, moulded, whitewashed screen with a date on it'.

note: Tranche 3, Cape cluster, 5 September 2026. Added by this tranche. This is the richest architectural description in the South African register rows read for this cluster, and it is the only one that describes a MOULDING PROFILE: 'the holbol style at its most beautiful, with convex edge mouldings continued onto the gable face and ending as fully developed scrolls'. Holbol -- hollow-and-round, concavo-convex -- is the profile the node names on Boschendal, and this is the register's own account of what it consists of.
